groups.title: VNC supplements and shared heads
groups.proposal: Extend ordinary supplementation from NNCs to complete VNC supplements while preserving shared subject, object, and possessor heads, optional in, recursion, and the principal selected by the Nahuatl structure.
groups.writingJob: Accept typed VNC Results as supplements, bind each selected subject, object, or possessor head by referent identity, preserve nested supplements, and keep optional whole-unit in and traditional fused spellings separate from grammatical role.
groups.readingJob: Show the VNC as a complete supplementary clause, trace its exact head, and keep literal Nahuatl clause weighting distinct from smoother English translations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the real head role, principal, order, and optional in only when more than one final composition remains possible; the application derives reference agreement, nesting, and spelling projections.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the Lesson 17–18 supplementation controls and clickable head links; do not add a VNC-supplement switch or infer hierarchy from English.

groups.title: Pronominal existentials and included reference
groups.proposal: Build the special plural demonstrative and interrogative existential constructions from typed pronominal NNCs and introduce included-reference supplementation as a distinct whole-clause relation.
groups.writingJob: Derive ihqueh plus demonstrative forms and frozen interrogative existential forms from their typed sources, preserve licensed person or number mismatches, and distinguish shared-referent contact from a whole adjoined clause serving as the included referent.
groups.readingJob: Expose the frozen existential structure, traditional solid spellings, contextual singular-or-plural nonhuman readings, and the point where the complete adjoined clause rather than one matching pronoun becomes the referent.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the demonstrative or interrogative source and chooses a genuinely contextual number or referent reading; the application derives existential morphology, frozen agreement, and shared-versus-included structure from typed Results.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse pronominal NNC source selection, context, and supplementation reference mode only where structurally open; do not expose frozen morphology or agreement exceptions as manual switches.

groups.title: Included subjects, possessors, and recursive clauses
groups.proposal: Apply included-reference supplementation to subject and possessor roles, including nested sentences and Canvas-authorized ca clauses, without erasing any internal shared-reference structure.
groups.writingJob: Attach the complete adjoined clause or sentence as an included subject or possessor, preserve internal supplementation recursively, and allow typed ca clauses and optional in in their licensed positions.
groups.readingJob: Show which entire clause is the referent of the principal head, where a shared-referent reading remains genuinely possible, and how internal and external supplement links nest.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses included versus shared reference only where Andrews preserves both analyses and chooses the real subject or possessor role when ambiguous; the application preserves all nested links and ca marking.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse reference mode, head role, recursive recapture, ca, and optional in conditionally; do not add a generic included-clause or recursion toggle.

groups.title: Speech, questions, and reported content
groups.proposal: Treat statements, questions, commands, and other utterances as included-reference objects of typed speech or questioning VNCs, preserving direct versus indirect speech and the exact internal sentence type.
groups.writingJob: Bind the complete utterance to the speech-action object head, preserve statement, question, command, or exclamation structure, and realize direct or indirect reporting without reconstructing content from quotation marks.
groups.readingJob: Show the silent or overt content head, the reporter's perspective, the internal sentence type, and the difference between exact direct speech and indirect report.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses direct or indirect speech and supplies the intended content Result; the application derives content binding, punctuation, mood, and sentence-type cues.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse speech directness and captured sentence Results; do not ask separately for content type when the captured Result already determines it.

groups.title: Causing and requesting content
groups.proposal: Attach complete caused or requested propositions as included-reference objects while preserving honorific formation, participant roles, and the difference between causing and requesting.
groups.writingJob: Use typed causing or requesting predicates to license the included proposition, maintain causer, causee, requester, and requested-action participants, and preserve any honorific or impersonal structure already present.
groups.readingJob: Trace the whole proposition to its object head and show how its internal subject differs from the matrix causer or requester.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the intended causing or requesting predicate and resolves only real participant ambiguity; the application derives the content relation and preserves existing honorific grammar.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse captured Results, object-head selection, and participant references; do not add causing, requesting, or honorific exception switches.

groups.title: Wishes and realizability
groups.proposal: Derive the mood and tense of included wish content from whether the desired event is realizable, presently impossible, or past counterfactual, while preserving negative-wish structure.
groups.writingJob: Bind the whole desired proposition to the wish predicate and select its licensed indicative, optative, or counterfactual shape from typed realizability, time, polarity, and participant facts.
groups.readingJob: Show why similar English want or wish translations correspond to different Nahuatl mood-tense structures and keep negative scope visible.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the intended realizability and time interpretation when context cannot determine it; the application derives mood, tense, marker, and reference consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the existing wish-realizability choice only when multiple grammatical outcomes remain; do not expose mood or tense as duplicate composition controls.

groups.title: Perception, cognition, and emotion content
groups.proposal: Attach perceived, known, believed, remembered, feared, or emotionally evaluated propositions as included objects while preserving their typed tense, participants, recursion, and contextual interpretation.
groups.writingJob: Use the principal predicate's semantic family and the captured proposition to validate perception, cognition, memory, and emotion content, including licensed present perception and nested supplementation.
groups.readingJob: Show the experiencer and content head, the whole proposition that fills it, and any tense or semantic distinction that English obscures.
groups.decisionSplit: The user selects the intended lexical predicate and resolves genuine contextual readings; the application derives content class, tense restrictions, participant binding, and nested structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse lexical Source, captured content, reference, and recursion controls; do not add generic perception, knowledge, or emotion toggles.

groups.title: Same-subject futures and rumored report
groups.proposal: Derive English infinitive-like readings from same-subject future supplementation and preserve the unique quil rumored-report construction, optional mach, and traditional quilmach spelling.
groups.writingJob: Validate same-subject future content for the licensed knowledge, remembering, forgetting, and trying predicates; separately require the unique typed quil frame for rumored reports and attach optional mach without treating spelling fusion as grammar.
groups.readingJob: Explain why an English infinitive remains a complete Nahuatl clause, distinguish tla-nequi incorporation from two-clause supplementation, and show the reporter's noncommitment in quil reports.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the intended principal predicate and chooses optional mach or licensed fusion only when it changes the desired projection; the application derives same-subject, future, rumor, and incorporation boundaries.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse shared subject, tense, report particle, and projection controls; do not add infinitive, rumor, or quilmach grammar switches.

groups.title: Deleted saying principals
groups.proposal: Offer deletion of a typed saying principal only when its speech-content and addressee relations are recoverable, including the adverb-only survivor, while preserving direct or indirect speech.
groups.writingJob: Validate the full speech-action source, its saying clause, shared speaker and addressee participants, and included utterance before deleting the saying principal; preserve the remaining speech-action or adverb as principal and retain the invisible content link.
groups.readingJob: Show the recoverable saying clause, the surviving principal or adverb, the reported proposition, and why the surface constituents are not directly related without the deleted node.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the full or licensed deleted surface and direct or indirect report where both remain possible; the application derives deletion kind from the captured Results and validates every hidden link.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the conditional deleted-principal route repaired in Lesson 18; do not expose saying, adverb-only, or deleted-node identity as free switches.
